problem: The text says 'Some syllabi call m the metric module and P the English module'. P is the diametral pitch, in teeth per inch. The English (inch) module is the reciprocal, 1/P = d/z with d in inches, and its unit is inches. Calling P the English module contradicts the standard definitions.
fix: In inch units the diametral pitch is P = z/d, in teeth per inch. The corresponding tooth-size index is the English module m_e = 1/P = d/z, in inches, so m = 25.4 × m_e = 25.4/P mm.

problem: 'The angle between the common normal at the pitch point and the common tangent' leaves the tangent undefined; a student can read it as the tangent to the tooth profile or to the line of centres.
fix: The pressure angle φ is the angle between the common normal to the two profiles at the pitch point (that is, the line of action) and the common tangent to the two pitch circles at the pitch point.

problem: The addendum circle and dedendum circle are never defined, but Exam trap 1 uses 'the addendum circle' and students need it for any drawing question. Tooth thickness and space width are also left out of a section titled nomenclature.
fix: Add: the addendum circle has diameter d_a = d + 2m; the dedendum circle has diameter d_f = d − 2.5m. Tooth thickness and space width on the pitch circle are each half the circular pitch, πm/2.

problem: 'The cutter removes material from the pinion root to avoid interference' reads as if undercutting is a cure. Undercutting is the damage that interference causes during generation; it is not done on purpose.
fix: Interference makes the cutter remove material from the pinion root that should have stayed there; this unwanted removal is undercutting and it weakens the tooth. The cures are a minimum number of teeth, a larger pressure angle or profile shift.
